clue.text: University dissertation's about down-and-out

indicators.note: about means the dissertation goes round the university's letter

parts.note: a dissertation is an academic paper

explanation.surface: A student's thesis concerns a homeless person.
explanation.definitionFit: A pauper is a very poor person, someone destitute, which is what down-and-out means as a noun.

clue.text: Force vehicle to speed up after Petty Officer left in charge

indicators.note: after says the reversed word comes last
up, in a down clue, says the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to race is to speed

explanation.surface: A navy petty officer left in charge urges a vehicle to go faster.
explanation.definitionFit: A police force uses patrol cars, so a police car is a vehicle belonging to the force.

clue.text: Copper replaces one, making patrol complete

indicators.note: replaces says the copper symbol takes the place of the letter for one

parts.note: a patrol is a small military unit
I is the Roman numeral one
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A policeman substitutes for one officer, completing the patrol.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper suggests a policeman, but it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncut means not shortened or edited, so whole and complete.

clue.text: Best phone company accepts ninety pounds

indicators.note: accepts says the phone company takes the numeral inside it

parts.note: EE is a British mobile phone network
XC is ninety in Roman numerals
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: The finest phone firm takes a ninety-pound payment.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to best someone is to outdo them, which is to excel or surpass.

clue.text: One tries to cause upset and turmoil — occasionally crossing line

indicators.note: crossing says the kept letters straddle the abbreviation for line
occasionally says only every other letter of turmoil is kept

explanation.surface: Someone stirring up upset and turmoil now and then crosses the line.
explanation.definitionFit: An internet troll posts provocative messages deliberately to anger and disrupt other people online.

clue.text: Looked like Greeks regularly exploited space up top

indicators.note: up top, in a down clue, says the space comes above the word for exploited
regularly says every second letter of Greeks is taken

parts.note: an em is a printers' unit of space
bled, as in bled dry, means exploited

explanation.surface: Greeks often made use of the space at the top of a building.
explanation.definitionFit: Resembled means was similar to, so looked like.

clue.text: Oddly Lou Reed's drug free, touring India — it's brilliant

indicators.note: Oddly says the odd-numbered letters of Lou are taken
touring says what is left goes round the letter for India
free says the drug letters are removed from the name

parts.note: taken as the singer's surname itself
E is ecstasy; both Es of Reed are the drug and both go
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Lou Reed, strangely, is off drugs while on tour in India: how bright.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing both Es from REED leaves RD; 'touring' puts I inside to give RID.
explanation.definitionFit: Lurid means glaringly vivid in colour, which is one sense of brilliant.

clue.text: Quiet film actor

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
a film is a thin layer

explanation.surface: A soft-spoken screen actor.
explanation.definitionFit: A player is a performer in a play, so an actor.

clue.text: Likely for highly attractive sort to pick up student

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: to pick up says the attractive one takes the student inside

parts.note: babe is slang for a very attractive person
L is a learner, from L-plates on cars

explanation.surface: A gorgeous person is likely to chat up a student.
explanation.definitionFit: Probable means likely to happen or be true.

clue.text: Optical illusion partly inverted colour

indicators.note: inverted says the hidden letters are read backwards
partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An optical illusion that turns a colour upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partly' hides CALIL across 'Optical illusion'; 'inverted' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilac is a pale purple shade, named after the flowering shrub.

clue.text: One opens either end of Chubb-lock with small band

parts.note: the end of Chubb-lock is either C or K, written out literally as C, OR, K
a crew is a band or gang of people

explanation.surface: Someone picks a Chubb lock, perhaps with a small gang of burglars.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'either end of Chubb-lock' literally: its end is C OR K. Chubb is a British lock brand.
explanation.definitionFit: A corkscrew is the tool that opens a wine bottle, drawing out its cork.

clue.text: Share with journalist

parts.note: a hack is a journalist

explanation.surface: Splitting a scoop with a reporter.
explanation.definitionFit: A fair whack is a fair portion, so whack is an informal word for a share.

clue.text: Craft group catch heartless bully out?

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are put out of order and rearranged
heartless says the middle letter of bully is taken away

explanation.surface: A question of whether to catch a nasty bully and throw him out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' drops the central L of BULLY to leave BULY; 'out' rearranges CATCH plus BULY.
explanation.definitionFit: A yacht club is a society of sailors, so a group organised around sailing craft.

clue.text: Bond's boss and assistant returned for films, TV etc

parts.note: M is James Bond's boss at MI6

indicators.note: returned says the word for assistant is read backwards

parts.note: an aide is an assistant

explanation.surface: James Bond's chief and a helper come back for the movies and television.
explanation.definitionFit: The media are the mass channels of communication, of which cinema and television are examples.

clue.text: Declined journalist on record — men become focus of smear

indicators.note: become says one set of letters turns into another in the build
on says the journalist is placed after, tacked onto, the record

parts.note: taken as the word record itself
ED, short for editor, is the crossword journalist
OR, other ranks, is the usual crossword term for ordinary soldiers or men

indicators.note: focus of says the central letter of smear is wanted

explanation.surface: An editor declined to speak on the record as men became the focus of a smear campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Focus of' is setter-speak for a word's central letter; 'men' are other ranks, a common crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To recede is to go back or diminish, as a tide or hairline does, so declined in that sense.

clue.text: Outlaw speed bumps on bendy road

indicators.note: bumps suggests jolting, so the letters of speed are knocked about
bendy says the letters of road are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Speed bumps on a winding road.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a reckless criminal, someone outside the law, an outlaw.

clue.text: Broadcast dramedy describing a fantasy

indicators.note: describing, in its sense of drawing round, says the rearranged letters go around a
Broadcast suggests scattering, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A broadcast comedy-drama that depicts a fantasy.
explanation.definitionFit: A daydream is a pleasant fantasy indulged while awake.

clue.text: Mass conflict fractures defence

indicators.note: fractures says war breaks into the word for mass

parts.note: bulk means mass or size
war is armed conflict

explanation.surface: A huge war smashes through a country's defences.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulwark is a defensive wall or rampart, and figuratively any safeguard.

clue.text: Publish landlord's overseas correspondence

parts.note: to air something is to make it public
a letter is someone who lets property, a landlord

explanation.surface: Making public the landlord's letters from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: An air letter is a lightweight sheet folded into its own envelope for airmail.
explanation.definitionFit: An airletter is a sheet sent by airmail, so a form of correspondence going overseas.

clue.text: Heard every instrument

indicators.note: Heard says the word is as listened to, not as spelt

parts.note: all means every

explanation.surface: Every musical instrument could be heard.
explanation.definitionFit: An awl is a pointed tool for piercing holes in leather, an instrument in the sense of an implement.

clue.text: Lazy model, cast

parts.note: to model clay is to work it into shape
to shy is to throw or cast, as at a coconut shy

explanation.surface: An idle fashion model and the whole cast too.
explanation.definitionFit: Workshy describes someone who avoids work, i.e. idle and lazy.

clue.text: Consider speaker's approach

indicators.note: speaker's says the word is as spoken, not as spelt

parts.note: a way is an approach or method

explanation.surface: Think about how the speaker came at the subject.
explanation.definitionFit: To weigh something up is to consider it carefully.

clue.text: Approve funny red nose

indicators.note: funny suggests something odd, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Giving a thumbs-up to a comic red nose, as on Comic Relief day.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse is to give backing or official sanction, i.e. to approve.

clue.text: On choppy seas, English surfer finally wipes out

indicators.note: On, in a down clue, says those letters sit on top of what follows
finally says the last letter of surfer is taken
choppy, like a rough sea, says the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An English surfer on choppy water finally falls off his board.
explanation.walkthrough: Wipes out looks like surfing slang for falling, but is the definition: deletes.
explanation.definitionFit: Erases means rubs out or deletes, so wipes out.

clue.text: Furious, old Rover's losing power

indicators.note: losing says the power letter is dropped

parts.note: rover is an old word for a pirate or sea robber
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A furious old dog called Rover loses his strength.
explanation.walkthrough: Rover looks like a dog's name, but a rover is an archaic pirate.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate means angry, a synonym of furious.

clue.text: Disgust American by rolling tongue

indicators.note: rolling says the language's name is turned over and read backwards

parts.note: Lapp is a language, tongue meaning language

explanation.surface: Revolted by an American rolling their tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal is to fill with horror or dismay, which is to disgust.

clue.text: Perhaps Tommy Cooper's floundering with idea for trick, ultimately

indicators.note: floundering suggests confusion, so the letters are mixed up
ultimately says the last letter of each of those words is taken

explanation.surface: The comedian Tommy Cooper flounders with an idea for a magic trick.
explanation.walkthrough: Tommy Cooper was a British comedy magician; here Tommy is The Who's rock opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Tommy is The Who's 1969 rock opera, so it is an example of the genre.

clue.text: Daughter in prison, revealing bum

indicators.note: in says the daughter letter goes inside

parts.note: a cage is a prison

explanation.surface: A daughter in jail shows her backside.
explanation.walkthrough: Bum is a verb here, to scrounge, not the British noun for buttocks.
explanation.definitionFit: To cadge is to scrounge or beg, which is what bum means as a verb.

clue.text: Gold coin and compass

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
a bit is a small coin, as in a threepenny bit

explanation.surface: A gold coin and a navigator's compass, as in pirate treasure.
explanation.definitionFit: Compass can mean scope or range, and an orbit is a sphere of influence or range.

clue.text: Random parking in ditch first and road after — this vehicle is South African

indicators.note: after says the road letters come last
in says the parking letter goes inside the ditch

parts.note: a ha-ha is a sunken ditch serving as a boundary
ZA is South Africa's international vehicle registration code

explanation.surface: Chaotic parking: car in a ditch, then on the road, a South African vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: A ha-ha is a hidden ditch on English country estates.
explanation.definitionFit: Haphazard means lacking plan or order, so random or chance.

clue.text: Order tabbouleh twice — in retrospect, somewhat steep

indicators.note: in retrospect, looking back, says the hidden run reads backwards
somewhat says only a part of the doubled word, straddling the join, is used
twice says the word tabbouleh is written out two times

parts.note: taken as the word itself, a Levantine salad

explanation.surface: Ordering tabbouleh twice seems, looking back, a bit pricey.
explanation.walkthrough: Writing TABBOULEHTABBOULEH, 'somewhat' hides EHTAB across the join; 'in retrospect' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To steep something is to soak it in liquid, which is to bathe it.

clue.text: Gentle hit, initially, Billy Liar's out of print

indicators.note: initially says the opening letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: Billy Liar, the novel, has gone out of print.
explanation.walkthrough: Billy Liar is a 1959 British novel by Keith Waterhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: In baseball a bloop is a weakly hit ball that just clears the infield, so a soft hit.

clue.text: No leads on the water boiler?

indicators.note: no leads says the first letter of each of the two words is removed

explanation.surface: A water boiler with no electric leads attached.
explanation.definitionFit: A boiler heats water, so it is a type of heating device.
